ruling.recommended_action: Refund the unexempted detour mileage ($6.77) to the rider as a Ryde voucher via RydeHELP; note the RD-1 breach on the driver's record (no account flag required).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat #1/#2 [F8][F9] is a polite pickup-arrangement-style request about a petrol stop; the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is defensive but not abusive, threatening or harassing, and there is no dangerous-driving or injury allegation. No SAFE-1/SAFE-2 trigger; safety_concern = none.

Route deviation (RydeTAXI, so meter fare — detour km enters the fare [F4][F7]). One off-route segment identified: F3, 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km [F3], part of the +4.8 km / +35% overall excess [F1].

Exemption analysis:
- RD-4 (reasonable cause): no traffic incident at all [F14]; the only traffic facts are speed bands 5 (40–49 km/h) on CEX and Kampong Bahru Road [F12][F13], which are free-flow band 5, not band 1–2, and in any case a band alone cannot exempt (RD-4(b)). No exemption on this ground.
- RD-3(a): the rider did agree to a stop, but neither chat message names any place (only "the petrol station just ahead") and there is no app-recorded stop; no fact ties the stop to the route actually driven, and the complaint says he never stopped for petrol anyway. A nameless "one minute" stop does not make a 21-minute, 6.27 km loop a rider-named stop [F8][F9].
- RD-5: consent was given before the segment began (21:36 < 21:39), but its scope is a short stop for petrol, not a long loop. The driver's own account [F11] confirms he treated it as licence for "a small change of route", which is exactly the over-reading the policy forbids. Consent to a one-minute petrol stop does not cover a 4.56 km off-route loop; driver errands (his own fuel run) are not covered (RD-5; G11 — his written assertion is a claim, not rider consent). Ground: scope_other / driver_errand → the segment counts as an unexempted detour (RD-1).

Amount (RD-2): the segment adds 4.56 km; the billed excess over the optimal route is 4.80 km × $1.4100/km = $6.77 [F4]. Refund the unexempted detour mileage = $6.77 as a voucher (NS-7). Note the billed waiting fee is only $0.11 for 0.4 min [F5], which is meter waiting time (RydeTAXI) and is not refunded; ride-time and base are meter-valid on a completed trip and are not contested items whose refund formula applies to waiting.

Flag: RD-6 requires the driver to have route disputes upheld in the last 90 days; the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld (2 upheld are other types) [F17], so no flag_account.

Confidence reduced slightly by the fact that the record shows no actual petrol stop, so the detour was purely the driver's errand; either way it is unexempted and the refund figure is unchanged.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message (21:36) agreed to a quick petrol stop [F8][F9]; consent covering a named/unnamed stop does not extend to a 6.27 km loop adding 4.56 km [F3]. RD-5 scopes consent to what was agreed; the driver's own account [F11] shows he read it as permission for a route change, which the words do not support. RD-4 gives no cover (speed band 5 [F12][F13], no incidents [F14]). No rider-named place ties the stop to the driven route (RD-3(a)). Segment counts as an unexempted detour under RD-1 → RD-2 refund of $6.77.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed to a route change is a claim, not rider consent; the only rider message (F9) agrees to a short petrol stop and does not cover the loop (RD-5, G11).
Driver's implicit reasonable-cause defence fails: no traffic incident (F14), and speed band 5 on CEX/Kampong Bahru (F12/F13) is free-flow, not band 1–2 congestion, and cannot exempt alone (RD-4).
